title: A single proportion with Wilson and Clopper-Pearson intervals
summary: Estimates a prevalence from a simple random sample, with the Wilson interval and the conservative Clopper-Pearson (exact) interval.
pinned_defaults: R: methods = 'wilson'. binom.confint defaults to 'all' and returns eleven intervals.
R: Clopper-Pearson from base binom.test, independent of the binom package.
Python: method='wilson'. proportion_confint defaults to 'normal', the Wald interval.
Python: method='beta' is Clopper-Pearson. statsmodels has no method named 'exact'.
_single_proportion_only: Wilson and Clopper-Pearson belong to a single proportion or rate from independent observations. Not to an odds ratio, a risk ratio or an adjusted model estimate, and not to clustered data, which takes a design-based interval (clustered-prevalence-cluster-sample).
